But first, can I have your telephone number, please? It's 03786 439 251.

Well, like I said, it's my back. OK.
Can you tell me which part of the back? Lower.
And have you had any problems with your back before? Yes.
I had a bit of trouble last year, in June, I think. Or was it July?
No, we went on holiday at the beginning of July, and it had cleared up by then.
And when did it start this time? Has it just come on?
No, I've had it, let's see, since Monday, so that's three days now.
But it wasn't too bad at first.
I mean, I could just about get around, though.
I couldn't drive the car or anything.
Then this afternoon, the pain suddenly got so bad that I went to bed.
I've been in bed since, but that hasn't helped.
And do you have any pain elsewhere?
In your stomach or abdomen, for example? No.
Now, have you any idea what caused the problem?
Well, I was tidying up my office, and I lifted a box up from the floor that was heavier than I thought, and I think that's what did it.
Yes, it's easily done, isn't it? So you're in bed now? Yes.
Have you tried applying heat to the back?
Yes, I've got a hot water bottle.
That's usually the first thing I try.
And have you taken any painkillers? Yes.
And other than that, you feel quite well? I do, yes. Right.

Wrap it up in a towel or something.

I haven't tried that before.
It can be useful sometimes.
Now, have you seen your doctor about this?
No, I just thought, well, everyone has back pain, but I've never had it as bad as this before.
I think you should go and see your doctor tomorrow, and she may be able to give you something to help. OK, I'll do that.
I'm actually feeling a bit better now. Good.
And you might get some advice from her about exercise.
That's often the best way of dealing with this sort of problem. OK, I'll ask her. Right.
Now, if you're worried about anything before tomorrow, you can always phone back.
Our lines are open 24 hours. Thanks very much.
Good evening.
It's good to see so many parents here.
Let me begin by explaining why we go to the outdoor education centre.
Well, by age 10, we feel the children are ready for a trip away from home but still in a safe environment and under the guidance of a familiar adult.
At the school, we strongly believe children should be encouraged to try different things and not give up when it gets difficult.
And that's what the centre is all about, having a go.
Anyway, to start with, the sleeping arrangements.
For some children, this will be their first time in a tent and away from home, so please prepare them.
You can do this just by making sure they have some early nights before we go.
Another thing, there's space for three children per tent so we can't guarantee your child will be in with their best friends.
So do make them aware of this.
Now, you should have received a list with the clothing the children will need in their backpack.
But there are some extras.
Please provide a packet of biscuits or maybe fruit bars.
But these need to go in the box in the school hall, not with the children.
Actually, what we do need in the backpacks are bags for cleaning up and for wet clothing, so plastic ones please.
A torch is a good idea, but don't worry about putting money in because there's nothing to buy.

so we have written names on bits of paper and pulled them out of the box.
